metadata.title: Skills that Matter for Success and Well-being in Adulthood (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD Skills Studies report draws on the 2023 Survey of Adult Skills conducted under the OECD Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC). The survey uses a complex, multi-stage sampling design to produce population-representative estimates across participating countries; analysts should therefore apply the provided sampling weights when estimating distributions and relationships. The report also relies on PIAAC proficiency measurement (literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving) and includes additional self-reported social and emotional skills; for proficiency scales, OECD/PIAAC practice typically uses plausible values or equivalent latent-score procedures, while for self-reports the same weighted estimation logic applies. Because this document excerpt does not specify the exact weight variable names or replicate-weight method, the precise implementation details (e.g., BRR/jackknife) cannot be extracted here, but the weighting principle for complex survey inference remains central.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Skills Studies report uses evidence from the 2023 Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC) to examine how adults’ social and emotional skills relate to a broad set of outcomes, including employment and wages, health, life satisfaction, and civic engagement. It positions social and emotional skills as complementary to cognitive skills (literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving), and emphasizes that the 2023 survey is the first PIAAC cycle to include self-reported measures of social and emotional skills alongside international proficiency assessments. The report’s contribution is primarily descriptive and interpretive: it documents how these skills are distributed across populations and discusses their associations with key life outcomes, rather than presenting a predictive ML modeling pipeline in the provided excerpt. Methodological details on weighting, plausible-values combination, missing-data handling, and any model performance metrics are not included in the excerpt, limiting extraction of technical parameters.
